Scalars and Vectors: A scalar has magnitude only (distance, speed, time, mass), while a vector has magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, acceleration, force). Distance is the total path length; displacement is the straight-line change in position from start to finish. Speed is distance over time; velocity is displacement over time. A vector is drawn as an arrow, and the vector -A has the same magnitude as A but the opposite direction. In one dimension a plus or minus sign shows direction. Perpendicular vectors combine with the Pythagorean theorem.
Vector Addition and Components: The resultant is the single vector equivalent to several vectors. Add graphically tip-to-tail, drawing the resultant from the first tail to the last tip. Vectors in the same direction add, and opposite ones subtract. A vector A at angle theta from the x-axis has components Ax = A cos(theta) and Ay = A sin(theta). To add by components, sum all x parts to get Rx and all y parts to get Ry, then R = sqrt(Rx^2 + Ry^2) and theta = tan^-1(Ry / Rx). Forces are in equilibrium when their resultant is zero.
Relative Velocity: Velocity depends on the observer's frame of reference. The velocity of A relative to C equals the velocity of A relative to B plus the velocity of B relative to C. A boat's velocity relative to shore is its velocity in the water plus the current, and a plane's ground velocity is its air velocity plus the wind. Add speeds in the same direction, subtract them in opposite directions, and use the Pythagorean theorem when they are perpendicular. Perpendicular motions are independent, so crossing time depends only on the speed across the river.
Projectile Motion Launched Horizontally: A projectile moves under gravity alone, following a parabola when air resistance is ignored. Horizontal and vertical motions are independent and share the same time. Horizontally the velocity is constant, x = vx t. Vertically the acceleration is g = 9.8 m/s^2 downward, so for a horizontal launch vy = g t and y = (1/2) g t^2. The fall time t = sqrt(2h / g) does not depend on the horizontal speed. The speed at any moment is v = sqrt(vx^2 + vy^2).
Projectile Motion Launched at an Angle: For a launch speed v at angle theta, the components are vx = v cos(theta) and vy = v sin(theta). Horizontal velocity stays constant, while vertical velocity changes at -g and is zero at the highest point. Time to the top is vy / g, total time of flight on level ground is 2 vy / g, maximum height is vy^2 / (2g), and range is v^2 sin(2 theta) / g. The range is greatest at 45 degrees, and complementary angles give equal ranges. At the top the speed equals vx, not zero.
